newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-NICKLAUS BREAKS SNEAD RECORD AT MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-NICKLAUS BREAKS SNEAD RECORD AT MASTERS.

text.p: Jack Nicklaus, the six-time winner of the Masters, added another Masters record to his collection when he shot 78 on Sunday to finish his 39th tournament at Augusta National.

Nicklaus surpassed the mark of 146 rounds played in Masters competition that had been held by Sam Snead. But Nicklaus was not pleased with his record-setting 147th round that completed a 72-hole total of 11-over 299.
"I played awful," said the 57-year-old Nicklaus, who had already owned 32 Masters records. "I actually wore out. I worked hard to get myself into shape, but I couldn't finish the tournament."

Two of Nicklaus's records -- widest margin of victory (nine shots in 1965) and lowest 72-hole total (271 in 1965) were in jeopardy, given Tiger Woods's amazing march toward victory at Augusta National.
Nicklaus said he was rooting for the 21-year-old Woods.
"Tiger is out there playing another game," Nicklaus said in appreciation. "He's playing a golf course he'll own for a long time. I really hope he plays well."
Nicklaus, who also won five PGA championships, four U.S. Opens and three British Opens, was not impressed by his latest Masters feat.
"It's just another old age mark," said Nicklaus before turning his thoughts back to Woods.
"It's not my time anymore," Nicklaus said. "It's his."
